description: This topic covers the meaning and importance of farm records, their main types, simple farm accounts and budgeting, and how good record keeping improves farm management and decision-making.

options.text: Written information about all activities and events taking place on the farm
Money kept in the bank by the farmer
The boundaries that separate one farm from another
Tools used for ploughing the land

mcq.explanation: Farm records are written or documented information about activities, inputs, outputs and events that occur on the farm.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a type of farm record that shows the quantity of crops or livestock products obtained?
mcq.explanation: Production records keep track of outputs such as kilograms of maize harvested or litres of milk produced.

mcq.questionText: A record that lists all the assets and property owned by the farm, such as machinery and stock of feeds, is called a:
mcq.explanation: An inventory record shows all the assets and items the farm owns and their quantities at a given time.

mcq.questionText: Which record would a dairy farmer use to track which cow was mated, by which bull, and the expected calving date?
mcq.explanation: Breeding records track mating, service dates, sires used and expected birth dates of animals.

mcq.questionText: Profit on a farm is calculated as:
mcq.explanation: Profit is the surplus that remains after subtracting all expenditure from total income.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is recorded as farm expenditure?

options.text: Income from renting out a tractor

mcq.explanation: Expenditure is money spent on inputs such as fertilizers, seeds, feeds and labour.

mcq.questionText: A labour record on a farm mainly shows:

options.text: The number of workers, hours worked and wages paid

mcq.explanation: Labour records keep details of workers employed, time worked and wages or salaries paid.

mcq.questionText: A farmer's income was 800,000 shillings and expenditure was 950,000 shillings in one season. The farm made a:
mcq.explanation: Since expenditure (950,000) is greater than income (800,000), the farm made a loss of 150,000 shillings.

mcq.questionText: A farm budget is best described as:

options.text: A record of past harvests only
A plan that estimates future income and expenditure
A list of all animals on the farm
A diary of daily weather conditions

mcq.explanation: A budget is a financial plan that estimates the expected income and expenditure of the farm over a future period.

mcq.questionText: Which field record helps a farmer know what crop was grown on each plot in previous seasons to plan crop rotation?
mcq.explanation: Field records show the history of each plot, including the crops grown and operations done, helping in planning rotation.

mcq.questionText: One importance of keeping farm records is that they help the farmer to:

options.text: Avoid paying any taxes at all
Make sound decisions and plan future farm activities
Stop pests from attacking crops automatically

mcq.explanation: Records provide information that guides the farmer in making informed decisions and planning future operations.

mcq.questionText: Why are accurate financial records important when a farmer wants a loan from a bank?

options.text: They prove the farm's income and ability to repay the loan
They guarantee that crops will never fail
They replace the need for any collateral entirely
They reduce the interest rate to zero

mcq.explanation: Banks use financial records to assess the profitability and creditworthiness of the farm before lending.

mcq.questionText: A farmer notices from records that one maize variety yields more per acre than another at the same cost. The records have mainly helped in:

options.text: Comparing performance to choose the better enterprise
Increasing the size of the farm land

mcq.explanation: Good records allow comparison of different enterprises or varieties so the farmer can select the most profitable one.

mcq.questionText: Which document summarizes total income and total expenditure to show whether the farm gained or lost over a period?
mcq.explanation: The profit and loss account compares income against expenditure to reveal profit or loss for the period.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a feature of well-kept farm records?

options.text: They are written neatly, accurately and kept up to date
They are kept only in the farmer's memory
They are filled with guesses and estimates only
They are updated once every ten years

mcq.explanation: Good records should be accurate, neat, simple, complete and regularly updated to be useful.

fib.questionText: Written information about all activities carried out on a farm is called farm _____.
fib.explanation: Farm records document the activities, inputs and outputs of the farm.

fib.questionText: The type of record that shows the quantity of milk, eggs or crops obtained is called a _____ record.
fib.explanation: Production records track the output produced by the farm enterprises.

fib.questionText: Money received by the farm from selling produce is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Income is the total money earned from farm sales and other receipts.

fib.questionText: Money spent on farm inputs such as seeds, fertilizers and feeds is called _____.
fib.explanation: Expenditure is the money paid out to run the farm.

fib.questionText: When total income is greater than total expenditure, the farm makes a _____.
fib.explanation: Profit occurs when income exceeds expenditure.

fib.questionText: A list of all assets and property owned by the farm is kept in an _____ record.
fib.explanation: Inventory records show the assets and their quantities owned by the farm.

fib.questionText: A financial plan that estimates expected future income and expenditure is called a farm _____.
fib.explanation: A budget helps the farmer plan ahead for income and spending.

fib.questionText: Records showing mating dates, sires used and expected calving dates of animals are called _____ records.
fib.explanation: Breeding records help in managing reproduction and improving stock.

fib.questionText: Records that show the number of workers, hours worked and wages paid are called _____ records.
fib.explanation: Labour records keep track of the workforce and their payments.

fib.questionText: The account that compares total income and total expenditure to show profit or loss is called the _____ account.
fib.explanation: The profit and loss account summarizes the financial result of the farm over a period.

tf.questionText: Farm records can be used to help the farmer make better decisions.
tf.explanation: Records provide information that guides planning and decision-making.

tf.questionText: Production records show the money spent on buying tractors only.
tf.explanation: Production records show outputs such as crops or livestock products, not purchases of machinery.

tf.questionText: Profit is obtained by subtracting total expenditure from total income.
tf.explanation: Profit equals total income minus total expenditure.

tf.questionText: If expenditure is greater than income, the farm has made a profit.
tf.explanation: When expenditure exceeds income, the farm makes a loss, not a profit.

tf.questionText: A budget is a plan that estimates future income and expenditure.
tf.explanation: Budgeting is forward planning of expected income and spending.

tf.questionText: Inventory records show all the assets and stock owned by the farm.
tf.explanation: Inventory records list the property and items the farm owns.

tf.questionText: Keeping records only in the farmer's memory is the best method of record keeping.
tf.explanation: Records should be written down accurately, since memory is unreliable and can be forgotten.

tf.questionText: Good farm records can help a farmer secure a loan from a financial institution.
tf.explanation: Banks use farm records to judge the farm's profitability and ability to repay.

tf.questionText: Breeding records are useful for tracking which animal was mated and when it is expected to give birth.
tf.explanation: Breeding records show service dates and expected birth dates of animals.

tf.questionText: Farm records have no use in comparing the performance of different enterprises.
tf.explanation: Records allow farmers to compare enterprises and choose the most profitable one.

summary.correctAnswer: Written information about all activities and events on the farm
summary.explanation: They document inputs, outputs and operations of the farm.

summary.correctAnswer: Records of outputs such as crops harvested and livestock products
summary.explanation: Examples include kilograms of maize and litres of milk.

summary.correctAnswer: Records of money received (income) and money spent (expenditure)
summary.explanation: They help calculate profit or loss.

summary.correctAnswer: Records listing the farm's assets and stock and their quantities
summary.explanation: Examples include machinery, tools and stored feeds.

summary.correctAnswer: Records of workers, hours worked and wages paid
summary.explanation: They help manage and pay the workforce.

summary.correctAnswer: Records of mating, sires used and expected birth dates of animals
summary.explanation: They help improve and manage livestock reproduction.

summary.correctAnswer: Profit = total income minus total expenditure
summary.explanation: A surplus shows profit; a deficit shows loss.

summary.correctAnswer: A plan estimating future farm income and expenditure
summary.explanation: It guides planning and use of resources.

summary.correctAnswer: They aid decision-making, planning, loan access and enterprise comparison
summary.explanation: Good records improve overall farm management.

summary.correctAnswer: Accurate, neat, simple, complete and regularly updated
summary.explanation: These qualities make records reliable and useful.

hoq.questionText: A farmer kept two enterprises last season. Poultry earned 1,200,000 shillings income with 700,000 shillings expenditure, while maize earned 900,000 shillings income with 800,000 shillings expenditure. Using farm records to compare, which decision is most justified?

options.text: Expand poultry because it gave a higher profit of 500,000 shillings
Expand maize because it gave a higher income
Drop both because both made losses
Keep them equal because profits are the same

hoq.explanation: Poultry profit is 1,200,000 - 700,000 = 500,000, while maize profit is 900,000 - 800,000 = 100,000, so expanding poultry is justified.

hoq.questionText: A farmer prepares a budget showing planned expenditure higher than expected income for the coming season. What is the most sensible action before starting?

options.text: Ignore the budget and continue as planned
Adjust the plan by cutting costs or raising expected income to avoid a loss
Stop keeping any records to save time

hoq.explanation: A budget that forecasts a loss signals the farmer to revise the plan by reducing costs or increasing income before committing resources.

hoq.questionText: A dairy farmer's production records show milk yield falling sharply for one cow over several weeks while feed remains the same. How do the records best help in decision-making?

options.text: They prove the cow will recover without any action
They reveal a problem early so the farmer can investigate health or breeding and act
They automatically increase the milk yield
They show the weather is the only cause

hoq.explanation: Trends in production records flag problems early, allowing the farmer to investigate causes such as disease and take timely corrective action.
